claim: SF3B1 is recurrently mutated in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)
source: The splicing factor SF3B1 is recurrently mutated in various tumors, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bailey et al., 2016 and Yang et al., 2021 in the introduction

claim: Sf3b1K700E alone is insufficient to induce malignant transformation of the murine pancreas
source: Here, we demonstrate that Sf3b1K700E alone is insufficient to induce malignant transformation of the murine pancreas
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing no effect on survival or pancreas weight after 300 days in Sf3b1K700E/+ mice

claim: Sf3b1K700E increases aggressiveness of PDAC when it co-occurs with mutated KRAS and p53
source: Here, we demonstrate that Sf3b1K700E alone is insufficient to induce malignant transformation of the murine pancreas, but that it increases aggressiveness of PDAC if it co-occurs with mutated KRAS and p53.
evidence: Supported by survival and tumor size data from KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice compared to KPC mice

claim: Sf3b1K700E plays a role during early stages of pancreatic tumor progression
source: We further show that Sf3b1K700E already plays a role during early stages of pancreatic tumor progression
evidence: Supported by data showing increased ADM formation and PDAC development in 5-week-old KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice and in KC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice

claim: Sf3b1K700E reduces the expression of TGF-β1-responsive epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) genes
source: We further show that Sf3b1K700E already plays a role during early stages of pancreatic tumor progression and reduces the expression of TGF-β1-responsive epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) genes.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data showing EMT as the most significantly attenuated gene set in KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ cells

claim: SF3B1K700E confers resistance to TGF-β1-induced cell death in pancreatic organoids and cell lines
source: Moreover, we found that SF3B1K700E confers resistance to TGF-β1-induced cell death in pancreatic organoids and cell lines
evidence: Supported by caspase activity assays and viability measurements in organoids and cell lines

claim: SF3B1K700E-mediated resistance to TGF-β1 is partly mediated through aberrant splicing of Map3k7
source: Moreover, we found that SF3B1K700E confers resistance to TGF-β1-induced cell death in pancreatic organoids and cell lines, partly mediated through aberrant splicing of Map3k7.
evidence: Supported by Map3k7 splicing analysis, knockdown experiments, and overexpression experiments

claim: SF3B1K700E acts as an oncogenic driver in PDAC
source: Overall, our findings demonstrate that SF3B1K700E acts as an oncogenic driver in PDAC
evidence: Supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence including mouse models, organoid studies, and molecular analyses

claim: SF3B1K700E promotes the progression of early stage tumors by impeding the cellular response to tumor suppressive effects of TGF-β
source: Overall, our findings demonstrate that SF3B1K700E acts as an oncogenic driver in PDAC, and suggest that it promotes the progression of early stage tumors by impeding the cellular response to tumor suppressive effects of TGF-β.
evidence: Supported by data showing reduced TGF-β-induced apoptosis and EMT in SF3B1K700E mutant cells

claim: SF3B1 is amongst the most commonly mutated components of the splicing machinery in cancer
source: The splicing factor subunit 3b 1 (SF3B1) is amongst the most commonly mutated components of the splicing machinery, with high incidence in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS; Je et al., 2013) and chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL; Miao et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to studies in MDS and CLL

claim: SF3B1 is recurrently mutated in uveal melanoma
source: However, also in various solid tumors, SF3B1 is recurrently mutated, including uveal melanoma (UVM; Furney et al., 2013)
evidence: Supported by citation to Furney et al., 2013

claim: SF3B1 is recurrently mutated in breast cancer
source: However, also in various solid tumors, SF3B1 is recurrently mutated, including uveal melanoma (UVM; Furney et al., 2013), breast cancer (BRCA; Fu et al., 2017; Maguire et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2020)
evidence: Supported by citations to Fu et al., 2017; Maguire et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2020

claim: SF3B1 is recurrently mutated in prolactinomas
source: However, also in various solid tumors, SF3B1 is recurrently mutated, including uveal melanoma (UVM; Furney et al., 2013), breast cancer (BRCA; Fu et al., 2017; Maguire et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2020), prolactinomas (Li et al., 2020)
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2020

claim: SF3B1 is recurrently mutated in hepatocellular carcinoma
source: However, also in various solid tumors, SF3B1 is recurrently mutated, including uveal melanoma (UVM; Furney et al., 2013), breast cancer (BRCA; Fu et al., 2017; Maguire et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2020), prolactinomas (Li et al., 2020), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; Zhao et al., 2021)
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2021

claim: SF3B1 is recurrently mutated in pancreatic adenocarcinoma
source: However, also in various solid tumors, SF3B1 is recurrently mutated, including uveal melanoma (UVM; Furney et al., 2013), breast cancer (BRCA; Fu et al., 2017; Maguire et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2020), prolactinomas (Li et al., 2020), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; Zhao et al., 2021), and pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC; Bailey et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bailey et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2021

claim: SF3B1 is part of the U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (U2 snRNP)
source: As part of the U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (U2 snRNP) SF3B1 exerts an essential function in RNA splicing by recognizing the branchpoint sequence (BPS) of nascent RNA transcripts (Wahl et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wahl et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2020

claim: SF3B1 recognizes the branchpoint sequence (BPS) of nascent RNA transcripts
source: As part of the U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (U2 snRNP) SF3B1 exerts an essential function in RNA splicing by recognizing the branchpoint sequence (BPS) of nascent RNA transcripts (Wahl et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wahl et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2020

claim: SF3B1 recognition of BPS is crucial for the definition of the 3' splice site of the upstream exon-intron boundary
source: This process is crucial for the definition of the 3' splice site (3' ss) of the upstream exon-intron boundary, a prerequisite for the accurate removal of introns (Wahl et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wahl et al., 2009

claim: Hotspot mutations in SF3B1 at HEAT repeats 5–9 allow the recognition of an alternative BPS
source: It is well understood that hotspot mutations in SF3B1 at HEAT repeats 5–9 allow the recognition of an alternative BPS, resulting in the inclusion of a short intronic region into the mature messenger RNA (mRNA; Alsafadi et al., 2016; Canbezdi et al., 2021; Darman et al., 2015; DeBoever et al., 2015; Kesarwani et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Alsafadi et al., 2016; Canbezdi et al., 2021; Darman et al., 2015; DeBoever et al., 2015; Kesarwani et al., 2017

claim: Alternatively spliced transcripts caused by SF3B1 mutations are prone to degradation through nonsense-mediated RNA decay (NMD)
source: These alternatively spliced transcripts are prone to degradation through nonsense-mediated RNA decay (NMD) (Darman et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Darman et al., 2015

claim: Missplicing of PPP2R5A by oncogenic SF3B1 increases malignancy through stabilizing c-Myc
source: So far, missplicing of PPP2R5A was found to increase malignancy through stabilizing c-Myc (Liu et al., 2020a; Yang et al., 2021)
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2020a; Yang et al., 2021

claim: Aberrant MAP3K7 splicing by oncogenic SF3B1 promotes NF-κB-driven tumorigenesis
source: and aberrant MAP3K7 splicing was reported to promote NF-κB-driven tumorigenesis (Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2021

claim: Splicing deregulation has been reported as a hallmark of PDAC
source: Since splicing deregulation has been reported as a hallmark of PDAC, with SF3B1 being recurrently mutated (Bailey et al., 2016)
evidence: Supported by citation to Bailey et al., 2016

claim: Genes encoding for the splice factors RBM10, SF3B1, and U2AF1 are frequently mutated in the Pancreatic Cancer Canadian (PACA-CA) cohort
source: Validating these findings, we found that genes encoding for the splice factors RBM10, SF3B1, and U2AF1 are also frequently mutated in the Pancreatic Cancer Canadian (PACA-CA) cohort (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: 56% of the mutations found in RBM10 lead to a truncated protein
source: In accordance with its described function as a tumor suppressor (Hernández et al., 2016), 56% of the mutations found in RBM10 lead to a truncated protein.
evidence: Supported by data analysis and citation to Hernández et al., 2016

claim: RBM10 functions as a tumor suppressor
source: In accordance with its described function as a tumor suppressor (Hernández et al., 2016), 56% of the mutations found in RBM10 lead to a truncated protein.
evidence: Supported by citation to Hernández et al., 2016

claim: The majority of mutations in SF3B1 and U2AF1 were missense mutations that occurred at hotspot sites
source: Conversely, in SF3B1 and U2AF1 the majority of mutations were missense mutations that occurred at hotspot sites, indicating a neomorphic function of the mutated proteins.
evidence: Supported by data analysis from PACA-CA cohort

claim: Missense mutations at hotspot sites in SF3B1 and U2AF1 indicate a neomorphic function of the mutated proteins
source: Conversely, in SF3B1 and U2AF1 the majority of mutations were missense mutations that occurred at hotspot sites, indicating a neomorphic function of the mutated proteins.
evidence: Inferred from the pattern of mutations observed

claim: The most frequently found mutation in SF3B1 in PDAC leads to a lysine (K) to glutamic acid (E) change at position 700
source: Like in other cancer types, also in PDAC the most frequently found mutation in SF3B1 led to a lysine (K) to glutamic acid (E) change at position 700 (SF3B1K700E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: Heterozygous activation of the Sf3b1K700E allele did not have any effect on survival of mice after 300 days
source: However, heterozygous activation of the Sf3b1K700E allele did not have any effect on survival of mice or weight of the pancreas after 300 days (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by survival data shown in Figure 1B and C

claim: Heterozygous activation of the Sf3b1K700E allele did not have any effect on weight of the pancreas after 300 days
source: However, heterozygous activation of the Sf3b1K700E allele did not have any effect on survival of mice or weight of the pancreas after 300 days (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by pancreas weight data shown in Figure 1B and C

claim: KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ animals displayed a significantly shorter survival compared to KPC mice
source: Importantly, KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ animals displayed a significantly shorter survival (mean survival 57 days vs. 64 days), and an increased tumor size compared to KPC mice at the age of 9 weeks (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: Supported by survival data shown in Figure 1E

claim: KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ animals displayed an increased tumor size compared to KPC mice at the age of 9 weeks
source: Importantly, KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ animals displayed a significantly shorter survival (mean survival 57 days vs. 64 days), and an increased tumor size compared to KPC mice at the age of 9 weeks (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: Supported by tumor size data shown in Figure 1F

claim: 67% of KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice vs. 25% of KPC mice developed PDAC at 5 weeks of age
source: Indeed, when we analyzed pancreata of 5-week-old mice, already 67% of KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice vs. 25% of KPC mice developed PDAC.
evidence: Supported by histological analysis of 5-week-old mice

claim: KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice showed an increase in acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) formation at 5 weeks of age
source: Moreover, we observed an increase in acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) formation and in the number of CK19 and MUC5AC positive cells, and a reduction in ß-amylase staining (Figure 1G–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1J, K).
evidence: Supported by histological data shown in Figure 1G-J and Figure 1—figure supplement 1J, K

claim: KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice showed an increase in the number of CK19 positive cells at 5 weeks of age
source: Moreover, we observed an increase in acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) formation and in the number of CK19 and MUC5AC positive cells, and a reduction in ß-amylase staining (Figure 1G–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1J, K).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G-J

claim: KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice showed an increase in the number of MUC5AC positive cells at 5 weeks of age
source: Moreover, we observed an increase in acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) formation and in the number of CK19 and MUC5AC positive cells, and a reduction in ß-amylase staining (Figure 1G–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1J, K).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G-J

claim: KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice showed a reduction in ß-amylase staining at 5 weeks of age
source: Moreover, we observed an increase in acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) formation and in the number of CK19 and MUC5AC positive cells, and a reduction in ß-amylase staining (Figure 1G–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1J, K).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G-J and Figure 1—figure supplement 1J, K

claim: At 43 weeks of age, the area of neoplastic pancreas tissue was increased in KC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice compared to KC mice
source: At 43 weeks of age, the area of neoplastic pancreas tissue was increased, and in 64% of KC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice vs. 10% of KC mice the lesions had already progressed to PDAC (Figure 1L; Figure 1—figure supplement 1L).
evidence: Supported by histological data shown in Figure 1L and Figure 1—figure supplement 1L

claim: 64% of KC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice vs. 10% of KC mice had lesions that progressed to PDAC at 43 weeks of age
source: At 43 weeks of age, the area of neoplastic pancreas tissue was increased, and in 64% of KC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice vs. 10% of KC mice the lesions had already progressed to PDAC (Figure 1L; Figure 1—figure supplement 1L).
evidence: Supported by histological data shown in Figure 1L

claim: The time of disease-free survival was significantly shortened in KC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice vs. KC mice
source: In addition, the time of disease-free survival was significantly shortened in KC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice vs. KC mice (Figure 1K).
evidence: Supported by survival data shown in Figure 1K

claim: In orthotopically transplanted KPC and KPC-Sf3b1K700E cells from fully developed PDAC tumors, no differences in tumor growth were observed
source: Finally, in a model for advanced cancer, where KPC and KPC-Sf3b1K700E cells were harvested from fully developed PDAC tumors and expanded in vitro before being orthotopically transplanted, we did not observe differences in tumor growth (Figure 1—figure supplement 1M, N).
evidence: Supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1M, N

claim: SF3B1K700E contributes to PDAC malignancy by accelerating the formation of precursor lesions
source: Together, our data demonstrate that the SF3B1K700E contributes to PDAC malignancy by accelerating the formation of precursor lesions.
evidence: Inferred from data showing effects in early stage tumors but not in advanced transplanted tumors

claim: Principal component analysis separated KPC and KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ sequenced replicates according to genotype
source: Principal component analysis separated the sequenced replicates (3 KPC and 4 KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ tumors) according to the genotype, indicating a major impact of the K700E mutation on the transcriptome (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by PCA data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B

claim: IFN-α-response was the most significantly enriched pathway in KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ tumor cells
source: We next performed gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), which revealed IFN-α-response as the most significantly enriched pathway in KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ tumor cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C

claim: Aberrant splicing caused by SF3B1 inhibition or oncogenic SF3B1 mutations induces an IFN-α-response through retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) mediated recognition of cytosolic aberrant RNA-species
source: This result is in line with a previous study, which found that aberrant splicing caused by SF3B1 inhibition or oncogenic SF3B1 mutations induces an IFN-α-response through retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) mediated recognition of cytosolic aberrant RNA-species (Chang et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chang et al., 2021

claim: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) emerged as the most significantly attenuated gene set in KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ cells
source: Interestingly, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) emerged as the most significantly attenuated gene set in KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ cells (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 2A, B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C

claim: Tenascin-C (Tnc) is downregulated in KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ tumors
source: We first confirmed downregulation of the most significantly depleted gene of the EMT gene set, the glycoprotein Tenascin-C (Tnc), by qPCR on additional KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ tumor samples (Figure 2C) and by histology in KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ PDAC sections (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and histology data shown in Figure 2C, D, and E

claim: 71% of the analysed EMT genes were significantly reduced in KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ vs. KPC organoids
source: Importantly, 71% of the analysed genes were significantly reduced in KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ vs. KPC organoids, with none of the genes showing a trend towards elevated expression (Figure 2F).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2F

claim: 55% of the analysed EMT genes were significantly downregulated in Sf3b1K700E vs. Sf3b1 WT organoids established from non-cancerous pancreata
source: Importantly, also in this experimental setup 55% of the analysed EMT genes were significantly downregulated in Sf3b1K700E vs. Sf3b1 WT organoids, with only one of the analysed genes showing a minor trend for elevated expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D

claim: Sf3b1K700E mediates downregulation of EMT-related genes in PDAC in a cell autonomous manner
source: Together, these data indicate that Sf3b1K700E mediates downregulation of EMT-related genes in PDAC a cell autonomous manner.
evidence: Inferred from organoid experiments showing EMT gene downregulation independent of tumor microenvironment

claim: 80% of the analysed EMT genes were strongly induced by TGF-β in tumour derived KPC cells
source: Importantly, we found that 80% of the analysed genes were strongly induced by TGF-β in tumour derived KPC cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E

claim: TNF-α significantly upregulated only 20% of the analysed EMT genes in KPC cells
source: whereas TNF-α significantly upregulated only 20% of these genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F

claim: In vitro induced Sf3b1K700E KPC cells fail or only partially induce 6 of the 9 assessed EMT genes when stimulated with TGF-β
source: Furthermore, we observed that in vitro induced Sf3b1K700E KPC cells fail or only partially induce 6 of the 9 assessed EMT genes when stimulated with TGF-β (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G

claim: In vitro induced Sf3b1K700E KPC organoids exhibit a sixfold decrease in matrigel invasion compared to KPC control organoids when stimulated with TGF-β
source: In line with these results, in vitro induced Sf3b1K700E KPC organoids exhibit a sixfold decrease in matrigel invasion compared to KPC control organoids when stimulated with TGF-β (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: Supported by invasion assay data shown in Figure 2G and H

claim: Human PANC-1 cells expressing SF3B1K700E display a reduced migratory rate compared to control PANC-1 cells expressing wildtype SF3B1 in a wound healing assay upon TGF-β stimulation
source: Moreover, human PANC-1 cells expressing SF3B1K700E display a reduced migratory rate compared to control PANC-1 cells expressing wildtype SF3B1 in a wound healing assay upon TGF-β stimulation (Figure 2I and J).
evidence: Supported by wound healing assay data shown in Figure 2I and J

claim: In pancreatic lesions TGF-β induces EMT, followed by apoptosis of the affected cells in a process termed lethal EMT
source: In pancreatic lesions TGF-β induces EMT, followed by apoptosis of the affected cells in a process termed lethal EMT (David et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to David et al., 2016

claim: The majority of apoptotic cells in KPC tumors reside in the lumen of PanINs
source: Performing immunofluorescence staining for cleaved caspase 3 in KPC tumors, we first confirmed that the majority of apoptotic cells reside in the lumen of PanINs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B)
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B

claim: Apoptotic cells in the lumen of PanINs are negative for the epithelial marker E-cadherin and positive for the mesenchymal marker Fibronectin-1
source: and that these cells are negative for the epithelial marker E-cadherin and positive for the mesenchymal marker Fibronectin-1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C; Hruban et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and citation to Hruban et al., 2006

claim: Sf3b1K700E tumors showed a reduction in luminally extruded cells
source: In line with our hypothesis, we observed a reduction in luminally extruded cells and a reduction in cleaved caspase 3-positive cells (CC3, Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by histological data shown in Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D

claim: Sf3b1K700E tumors showed a reduction in cleaved caspase 3-positive cells
source: In line with our hypothesis, we observed a reduction in luminally extruded cells and a reduction in cleaved caspase 3-positive cells (CC3, Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D

claim: Sf3b1 mutant KPC tumor organoids showed reduced cleaved caspase 3 and 7 activity when exposed to TGF-β1
source: To further analyse the impact of Sf3b1K700E on the tumor suppressive effect of TGF-β, we exposed Sf3b1 WT and Sf3b1K700E KPC tumor organoids to TGF-β1. We again observed reduced cleaved caspase 3 and 7 activity in Sf3b1 mutant organoids, and a greatly increased survival rate (72% vs 17% surviving organoids, Figure 3C–E).
evidence: Supported by caspase activity assay data shown in Figure 3C-E

claim: 72% of Sf3b1K700E KPC tumor organoids vs 17% of WT KPC tumor organoids survived TGF-β1 treatment
source: We again observed reduced cleaved caspase 3 and 7 activity in Sf3b1 mutant organoids, and a greatly increased survival rate (72% vs 17% surviving organoids, Figure 3C–E).
evidence: Supported by organoid viability data shown in Figure 3C-E

claim: Treatment with TGF-β1 led to significantly lower caspase 3 and 7 activity in Sf3b1K700E/+ vs. wildtype non-cancerous pancreatic organoids
source: While Sf3b1K700E led to slightly reduced proliferation without supplementation of TGF-β1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), treatment with TGF-β1 led to significantly lower caspase 3 and 7 activity in Sf3b1K700E/+ vs. wildtype organoids and to significantly enhanced survival (77% vs 3%) (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: Supported by caspase activity assay data shown in Figure 3F-H

claim: 77% of Sf3b1K700E/+ non-cancerous organoids vs 3% of WT non-cancerous organoids survived TGF-β1 treatment
source: While Sf3b1K700E led to slightly reduced proliferation without supplementation of TGF-β1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), treatment with TGF-β1 led to significantly lower caspase 3 and 7 activity in Sf3b1K700E/+ vs. wildtype organoids and to significantly enhanced survival (77% vs 3%) (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: Supported by organoid viability data shown in Figure 3F-H

claim: Exposure to low levels of TGF-β1 allowed long-term expansion of Sf3b1K700E/+ organoids for over 120 days, while the number of Sf3b1 WT organoids rapidly declined within the first 15 days
source: Finally, exposure to low levels (1 ng/ml and 2 ng/ml) of TGF-β1 also allowed long-term expansion of Sf3b1K700E/+ organoids (analysed for over 120 days), while the number of Sf3b1 WT organoids rapidly declined within the first 15 days (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1G, H).
evidence: Supported by long-term organoid culture data shown in Figure 3I and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G, H

claim: Overexpression of mutant SF3B1K700E resulted in increased viability upon TGF-β1 exposure compared to overexpression of wildtype SF3B1 in human H6c7 pancreatic duct cells
source: In line with our results from murine PDAC, overexpression of mutant SF3B1K700E resulted in an increased viability upon TGF-β1 exposure compared to overexpression of wildtype SF3B1 (Figure 3J)
evidence: Supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 3J

claim: SF3B1K700E had no effect on proliferation in absence of TGF-β1 treatment in human pancreatic duct cells and PDAC cell lines
source: while no effect of SF3B1K700E on proliferation was observed in absence of TGF-β1 treatment in human pancreatic duct cells and PDAC cell lines (Figure 3—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: Supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1J

claim: SF3B1K700E predominantly causes alternative 3' splice events in KPC tumor cells
source: By analysing RNA-seq data from sorted KPC vs. KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ tumor cells we predominantly identified alternative 3' splice events (Figure 4A, Supplementary file 2)
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq splicing analysis shown in Figure 4A

claim: Cryptic 3' splice sites in SF3B1K700E mutant cells show an upstream adenosine enrichment
source: with cryptic 3' ss showing an upstream adenosine enrichment and a less pronounced polypyrimidine tract most frequently located 8–14 bases upstream of the canonical 3' ss (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: Supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 4B and C

claim: Cryptic 3' splice sites in SF3B1K700E mutant cells show a less pronounced polypyrimidine tract
source: with cryptic 3' ss showing an upstream adenosine enrichment and a less pronounced polypyrimidine tract most frequently located 8–14 bases upstream of the canonical 3' ss (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: Supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 4B and C

claim: Cryptic 3' splice sites in SF3B1K700E mutant cells are most frequently located 8–14 bases upstream of the canonical 3' ss
source: with cryptic 3' ss showing an upstream adenosine enrichment and a less pronounced polypyrimidine tract most frequently located 8–14 bases upstream of the canonical 3' ss (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: Supported by distance analysis shown in Figure 4B and C

claim: SF3B1K700E-dependent alternative splice events in mice are consistent with previous splice-analyses performed in various murine SF3B1 mutant tissues
source: These findings are in accordance with previous splice-analyses performed in various murine SF3B1 mutant tissues (Liu et al., 2021; Mupo et al., 2017; Obeng et al., 2016; Yin et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2021; Mupo et al., 2017; Obeng et al., 2016; Yin et al., 2019

claim: In human cancers the SF3B1K700E hotspot mutation leads to a predominant use of cryptic 3' ss
source: In agreement with previous studies, we found that also in human cancers the SF3B1K700E hotspot mutation leads to a predominant use of cryptic 3' ss (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B, Supplementary file 2; Alsafadi et al., 2016; DeBoever et al., 2015; Kesarwani et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by pan-cancer analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B and citations

claim: 11 genes contained an alternative 3' splice-event linked to SF3B1K700E in both human tumors and KPC mice
source: Importantly, we further identified 11 genes that contained an alternative 3' splice-event linked to SF3B1K700E in human tumors as well as in KPC mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by comparative analysis shown in Figure 4D

claim: One third of Map3k7 transcripts were misspliced in pancreata of Sf3b1K700E/+ and KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice
source: Using targeted RNA-seq, we discovered that one third of Map3k7 transcripts were misspliced in pancreata of Sf3b1K700E/+ and KPC-Sf3b1K700E/+ mice (Figure 4E and F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by targeted RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4E, F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C

claim: MAP3K7 was misspliced in H6c7 cells and human PDAC cell lines overexpressing SF3B1K700E
source: Confirming inter-species conservation of this alternative splice-event, MAP3K7 was also misspliced in H6c7 cells and human PDAC cell lines overexpressing SF3B1K700E (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D

claim: No significant alternative 3'ss usage or mRNA expression of Ppp2r5a was observed in KPC-Sf3b1K700E tumor cells
source: Notably, when we further assessed SF3B1K700E dependent alternative splicing of Ppp2r5a, which was reported to impair apoptosis via post-translational modification of BCL2 in leukaemia (Liu et al., 2020a), we did not observe significant alternative 3'ss usage or mRNA expression of Ppp2r5a in KPC-Sf3b1K700E tumor cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR and RT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E, F

claim: Ppp2r5a missplicing shows tissue-specificity

claim: SF3B1K700E promotes PDAC progression by reducing tumor-suppressive TGF-β signalling through missplicing of MAP3K7
source: Taken together, this study provides a first demonstration that oncogenic SF3B1K700E promotes tumor progression in vivo in a mouse model for PDAC. Based on data from pancreatic organoids and cell lines, we further suggest that SF3B1K700E promotes PDAC progression by reducing tumor-suppressive TGF-β signalling through missplicing of MAP3K7.
evidence: Supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence from mouse models, organoids, and cell lines
